messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer 'AcmePay' is seeing tool-call args get cut mid-JSON during streaming. Their app errors with schema validation because the JSON ends with an open brace. Sample from their capture: `{"tool":"charge_card","args":{"amount":199.99,"currency":"USD",` and then stream closes.

aj: :eyes: Do we have a repro or raw bytes from their capture?

maria: They provided the raw chunk dump and a curl example. Their curl: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d '{"model":"r-infer","stream":true, ...}'` The raw server-side capture shows the chunk boundary splits inside the args.

suresh: Can you paste the raw chunk text? If it's splitting on a byte boundary it could be the proxy or our chunker.

maria: Raw snippet: `2c\r\n{"tool":"charge_card","args":{"amount":199.99,"currency":"USD",\r\n` — so the second chunk starts mid-object. Customer is using a downstream edge proxy (Fastly) in front of their client.

kevin: Two likely causes: 1) our streaming emitter is writing partial JSON across multiple SSE/data events (client libs sometimes expect one JSON object per event), or 2) intermediary is re-chunking at arbitrary sizes and the client parser isn't reassembling. Both can result in a truncated parse.

lisa: Quick mitigation: ask customer to disable proxy buffering or enable request body reassembly on the client side. Also they can switch to non-streaming mode for critical payment ops.

aj: Longer-term, we should be defensive in the runtime: reassemble incoming bytes before handing to the JSON schema validator. Can we buffer until full parseable JSON or an explicit end sentinel?

suresh: Implementation note: buffering until parse success is simple but defeats streaming semantics. Alternative: ensure our SSE/data boundaries align with top-level JSON token boundaries when emitting tool args. That requires a streaming-safe serializer that emits full top-level objects in one event.

maria: Customer accepted a temporary sentinel workaround: they appended an end-marker to the last event (`{\"__end_of_tool_args\":true}`) so their parser can detect completion. They're okay to wait for a patch but want ETA.

kevin: Plan: eng-runtime will push a fix to the SSE packager to avoid splitting top-level JSON objects across events and add a reassembly fallback for malformed-final-chunk detection. Target: hotfix in v1.2.3 next week, followed by a more robust fix in v1.3.

aj: For the support ticket can you collect the request id, customer org id, and the proxied request/response hex? We need to repro behind Fastly/envoy.

maria: Request id: req_0abc1234, org: acmepay-prod. I've uploaded the full chunk dump and the curl commands to the ticket.

suresh: Repro steps for eng: run local stream backend with `--sse` behind envoy with default buffer settings, then send a toolcall with a ~20KB args blob. See whether envoy reshapes chunks mid-brace.

kevin: Also add unit test that simulates a chunk split on a Unicode multi-byte boundary — some parsers can mis-handle partial UTF-8.

lisa: :thumbsup: Glad customer has workaround. Keep me posted on the hotfix PR.

aj: Filed follow-up task: INF-5678 to implement packager change + telemetry for incomplete-json errors.

maria: Closing loop with customer now — mentioning ETA and workaround. Thanks everyone.
